name: How long does an interior restoration project usually take?

mainEntity.name: How long does an interior restoration project usually take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The timeline depends on the scale of the damage, the drying requirements, and the types of materials involved. Simple drywall repairs, patching, and repainting in a single room typically take three to five business days once the area is dry. Extensive restorations involving damaged framing, subfloor replacement, tile work, or entire basements often take several weeks. A major factor affecting timing is scheduling sub-trades for required electrical and plumbing rough-ins before closing up walls with insulation and drywall. Working with a general contractor who oversees the entire job from framing to finish carpentry keeps the sequence moving efficiently.
acceptedAnswer.description: Small drywall and painting repairs take three to five days once dry, while extensive restorations involving framing, tile, and trade work take several weeks depending on scope.
